problem_text: For each nonnegative integer r less than 502, define S_r = sum of C(10000, k) over all k with 0 ≤ k ≤ 10000 and k - r a multiple of 502, where C(10000, n) = 0 when n > 10000. Find the number of integers in the list S_0, S_1, ..., S_501 that are multiples of the prime number 503.
notes: p=503, N=10000, d=p-1=502. S_r = sum C(10000,k) for k≡r (mod 502). 10000 = 19×502 + 462, so by Fermat/Lucas: S_r ≡ C(462,r) (mod 503). For 0≤r≤462: C(462,r)≢0 (mod 503) since 503 prime and 462<503. For 463≤r≤501: C(462,r)=0 so S_r≡0 (mod 503). Count = 501-463+1 = 39. Verified by direct computation (all 502 values of S_r mod 503).
